skill.name: convex-performance-audit
skill.description: Audits Convex application performance by tracing hot-path reads, write contention, subscription cost, and function budget pressure. It guides targeted fixes for slow or expensive Convex features.
skill.summary: Audit Convex performance signals and apply focused fixes for reads, writes, subscriptions, and function limits.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans and Convex ctx.db examples. Two findings are confirmed because the skill instructs agents to run npx Convex CLI diagnostics, including an @latest fallback. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx convex insights or any command that contacts a Convex deployment.
Prefer the project-local Convex CLI or a pinned package version instead of npx -y convex@latest.
Document which deployment flag is being used before collecting insights, especially for production, preview, or named deployments.

content.value_statement: Slow Convex features waste reads, trigger broad invalidations, and hide contention. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through targeted performance audits.
actual_capabilities: Routes performance symptoms to hot-path, contention, subscription, or function-budget checks.
Uses Convex insights output when available to prioritize expensive functions.
Traces read sets, write sets, indexes, subscriptions, and invalidation sources.
Recommends focused fixes such as indexes, digest tables, batching, and point-in-time reads.
Checks sibling functions that touch the same tables or derived data.
Adds verification steps for behavior, fallback safety, and reduced work.
limitations: Requires project code, runtime metrics, or user-provided symptoms for best results.
Does not replace load testing or production observability.
Large structural fixes may require separate migration planning.
Convex limits can change, so official documentation should be checked.

use_cases.title: Reduce Slow Query Cost
use_cases.description: Find unbounded reads, missing indexes, large row shapes, and unnecessary joins on a hot Convex path.

use_cases.title: Improve Reactive UI Performance
use_cases.description: Review subscriptions, query granularity, and invalidation patterns that cause sluggish Convex screens.

use_cases.title: Investigate Contention and Limits
use_cases.description: Analyze OCC conflicts, large mutations, function timeouts, and transaction budget pressure.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Slow Convex Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit with a clear symptom.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Convex feature for performance. Start from the slow user flow. Identify expensive reads, writes, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Subscription Cost
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for sluggish reactive pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page for unnecessary Convex subscriptions. Compare live freshness needs with point-in-time reads. Suggest focused changes and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve OCC Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Convex mutations for OCC conflicts. Find hot documents, broad read sets, no-op writes, and safe scheduling opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Performance Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cross-flow audit before broad edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Convex performance refactor plan across these related functions. Include migration risks, sibling paths, rollout order, and verification criteria.

output_examples.input: A project list loads slowly and reads many documents.
output: The audit identifies an unbounded list read and missing storage-side filtering.
It recommends an index-backed query, smaller return shape, and sibling list review.
Verification includes equal results and lower documents read in Convex insights.

output_examples.input: A dashboard feels sluggish after users scroll through several pages.
output: The review separates backend subscription cost from UI churn.
It suggests limiting live pages or using point-in-time fetching where freshness is low.
Verification checks subscription count, render frequency, and user-visible behavior.

output_examples.input: Mutations show OCC conflicts during busy voting periods.
output: The audit finds a hot counter document and competing writes.
It recommends sharding the counter or scheduling non-critical bookkeeping.
Verification checks conflict rate, latency, and data correctness.

best_practices: Start with measured signals before proposing structural changes.
Trace sibling readers and writers that touch the same tables.
Verify behavior and performance after every optimization.
anti_patterns: Do not replace simple scans when the table is small and the signal is weak.
Do not add digest tables without a hot path or large row shape.
Do not switch reactive views to point-in-time reads when live freshness matters.

faq.question: Does this skill run Convex commands automatically?
faq.answer: It can recommend Convex CLI diagnostics. Agents should ask before running external commands.

faq.question: Can it fix every performance problem?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on common Convex read, write, subscription, and function-budget patterns.

faq.question: Does it require production access?
faq.answer: No. It can audit code alone, but runtime insights make prioritization more reliable.

faq.question: Will it recommend migrations?
faq.answer: Only when the performance signal justifies a structural change or rollout risk exists.

faq.question: Is it useful for new Convex projects?
faq.answer: It is best after a feature has measurable slowness, cost, contention, or scale concerns.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
